children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 🌿 Complete Git & Version Control Engineering Track

Welcome to your full Git learning workspace materialized with **Trak**.

## 📚 Comprehensive Module Index

| Module | Title | Key Topics Covered |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-git-internals` | **Git Object Model** | `.git/` anatomy, Content-Addressable Storage (Blobs, Trees, Commits, Tags), SHA-1/SHA-256 |
| `01-three-trees-and-staging-lifecycle` | **The Three Trees** | Working Directory, Index (Staging), Commit History, `git add -p`, `git status` |
| `02-commit-mechanics-and-history` | **Atomic Commits & Log**| Conventional commits, `git commit --amend`, `git log --graph --oneline`, `git diff --staged` |
| `03-branching-and-pointer-mechanics`| **Branch Pointers** | Branches as 41-byte pointers in `refs/heads/`, `git switch -c`, Detached HEAD |
| `04-merging-fast-forward-vs-three-way`| **Merging Strategies**| Fast-Forward vs 3-Way merge, merge conflicts, `git merge --abort` |
| `05-rebasing-interactive-and-squash` | **Interactive Rebasing**| `git rebase -i HEAD~N` (squash, fixup, reword), The Golden Rule of Rebasing |
| `06-stashing-and-worktrees` | **Stashing & Worktrees**| `git stash pop`, `git worktree add` (parallel branch workspaces without switching) |
| `07-undoing-changes-reset-revert` | **Undoing History** | `git restore`, `git reset` (--soft, --mixed, --hard), `git revert` (safe public undo) |
| `08-reflog-and-disaster-recovery` | **Reflog Recovery** | `git reflog`, recovering deleted branches and commits after `reset --hard` |
| `09-cherry-picking-and-bisect` | **Cherry-Pick & Bisect**| `git cherry-pick`, Binary search bug hunting with `git bisect run` |
| `10-remotes-tracking-and-upstream` | **Remotes & Push Safety**| `git fetch` vs `git pull --rebase`, `git push --force-with-lease` |
| `11-tagging-and-semantic-versioning`| **Semantic Tagging** | Lightweight vs Annotated tags (`git tag -a`), SemVer (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) |
| `12-submodules-and-subtrees` | **Submodules & Subtrees**| `.gitmodules`, `git submodule update --init --recursive`, nested repos |
| `13-git-hooks-and-automation` | **Git Hooks Automation**| Client-side hooks (`pre-commit`, `commit-msg`), Husky integration |
| `14-git-attributes-and-lfs` | **Attributes & Git LFS**| `.gitattributes`, line-ending LF normalization, Large File Storage (LFS) |
| `15-gpg-signing-and-commit-security`| **Cryptographic Signing**| GPG / SSH commit signing, `git commit -S`, GitHub Verified commits |
| `16-advanced-workflows-trunk-based` | **Branching Workflows** | Trunk-Based Development vs GitHub Flow vs GitFlow, PR review strategies |
| `17-interview-questions-and-drills` | **Interview Master Drill**| Top 10 Git interview questions, resolving detached HEAD, and rebase disasters |

---

## 🛠️ Quick Commands

```bash
# Inspect Git commit graph:
git log --graph --oneline --decorate --all

# Safe force push:
git push --force-with-lease
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 00 - Git Object Model & Internals 🛠️

### Git's 4 Core Object Types in `.git/objects/`:
1. **Blob**: Stores raw file content (indexed by SHA-1/SHA-256 hash; does NOT store filename or permissions!).
2. **Tree**: Directory structure containing list of blobs/trees with filenames and mode permissions.
3. **Commit**: Points to a root Tree, parent commit(s), author, committer, and commit message.
4. **Tag**: Annotated reference pointing to a specific commit object with a message and GPG signature.

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 01 - The Three Trees Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────┐       ┌──────────────────────┐       ┌──────────────────────┐
│   Working Directory    │ ────► │     Staging Area     │ ────► │    Git Repository    │
│ (Your actual files)    │ <git  │ (Index - Binary Map) │ <git  │ (Immutable Commits)  │
│                        │ add>  │                      │ commit│                      │
└────────────────────────┘       └──────────────────────┘       └──────────────────────┘
```

```bash
# Stage individual hunks/patches interactively
git add -p
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 02 - Commit Mechanics & Conventional Commits

### Conventional Commit Format:
```
<type>(<optional scope>): <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```
Types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`.

```bash
# Amend the most recent commit without changing message
git commit --amend --no-edit
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 03 - Branching & HEAD Pointer Mechanics

A Git branch is **not a container of commits**; it is simply a 41-byte text file in `.git/refs/heads/<branch>` containing the 40-character SHA hash of its tip commit!

```bash
# Modern switch command
git switch -c feature/new-api

# Return to previous branch
git switch -
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 04 - Merging Strategies

- **Fast-Forward Merge**: Simply advances branch pointer forward when target branch has no divergent commits.
- **3-Way Merge (ORT Merge Engine)**: Creates a new merge commit with 2 parents by finding the Common Ancestor (Base).

```bash
# Force a merge commit even if fast-forward is possible
git merge --no-ff feature/auth
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 05 - Interactive Rebasing & Squashing

Rebasing replays a series of commits on top of a new base commit, creating a clean linear commit history.

```bash
# Rebase last 3 commits interactively
git rebase -i HEAD~3

# Auto-squash fixup commits
git commit --fixup <commit-hash>
git rebase -i --autosquash <base-branch>
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 06 - Git Worktrees (Zero Context-Switching)

Instead of stashing changes and switching branches, **Git Worktrees** allow checking out multiple branches simultaneously into separate directories:

```bash
# Check out hotfix branch in a parallel folder
git worktree add ../hotfix-worktree hotfix/urgent-bug

# List active worktrees
git worktree list

# Remove worktree when finished
git worktree remove ../hotfix-worktree
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 07 - Reset vs Revert vs Restore

| Command | Working Dir | Staging Area | History / HEAD | Safe on Public Branches? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`git restore <file>`** | Discards edits | Untouched | Untouched | **Yes** |
| **`git reset --soft HEAD~1`** | Preserves edits | Preserves edits | Moves HEAD back 1 commit | **No** (Local only) |
| **`git reset --mixed HEAD~1`**| Preserves edits | Unstages edits | Moves HEAD back 1 commit | **No** (Local only) |
| **`git reset --hard HEAD~1`** | **Wipes edits** | **Wipes edits** | Moves HEAD back 1 commit | **No** (Dangerous!) |
| **`git revert <commit>`** | Clean apply | Clean apply | **Appends new inverse commit** | **YES (Recommended)** |

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 08 - The Reflog: Git's Safety Net

The Reference Log (`git reflog`) tracks every single movement of `HEAD` for 90 days, enabling recovery of deleted branches and commits even after `git reset --hard`.

```bash
# 1. View reflog history
git reflog

# 2. Restore deleted branch from its last HEAD position
git branch restored-feature HEAD@{2}
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 09 - Git Bisect Automated Bug Hunting

`git bisect` uses binary search to pinpoint the exact commit that introduced a regression among thousands of commits:

```bash
git bisect start
git bisect bad                 # Current HEAD is broken
git bisect good v1.0.0         # v1.0.0 was working

# Automated bisect testing:
git bisect run npm test
```

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 10 - Remotes & Safe Force Pushing

Never use raw `git push --force` because it will overwrite teammates' commits. Always use:
```bash
git push --force-with-lease
```
This verifies that nobody else has pushed commits to the remote branch before overwriting.

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 16 - Trunk-Based Development vs GitFlow

- **Trunk-Based Development**: Short-lived feature branches (< 1-2 days) merged frequently into `main` behind feature flags. Recommended for modern CI/CD.
- **GitFlow**: Long-lived `develop`, `release/*`, `hotfix/*`, and `main` branches with heavy merge gates.

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 17 - High-Yield Git & Version Control Interview Questions 🎯

### Top 5 Interview Questions:
1. **Git Object Model**: Blobs store file data, Trees store directory hierarchies and filenames, Commits link trees with metadata and parent hashes.
2. **Rebase vs Merge**: Merge preserves full non-linear historical context with 2-parent commits; Rebase produces a clean, linear commit log by replaying commits on top of the target base.
3. **Reset vs Revert**: `reset` rewrites commit history locally; `revert` creates a new inverse commit preserving complete audit history on public branches.
4. **Worktrees**: Allows working on multiple branches simultaneously across separate directory trees without switching or stashing.
5. **--force-with-lease**: Safe atomic force-push that checks if remote branch tip matches our local tracking ref before overwriting.

🚀 You have completed the complete Git & Version Control Engineering track!
